facts.text: Chandler Heights sprang to life in 1928 when Chandler Heights Citrus, Incorporated—backed by Dr.—planted its first citrus grove.
Chandler Heights sits on the edge of Queen Creek’s planning zone, making most of its land a candidate for future annexation.
Proximity to San Tan Mountains creates microclimates with slightly cooler temperatures and varied topography, influencing local wind patterns and vegetation distribution.
Over decades, Chandler Heights has slowly urbanized, with recent annexations of land along Chandler Heights Road into Chandler and Queen Creek fueling growth.
Sandy loam soil, boosted by historic irrigation, once fed citrus farms, yet remains nutrient‑poor and alkaline like typical desert ground.
Chandler Heights is located approximately 13 miles southeast of Chandler and near Queen Creek in the southeastern Phoenix metro area.
